name: Isolated Cerebellar Agenesis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic criteria for isolated cerebellar agenesis

criteria.description: Neuroimaging (MRI) demonstrating complete absence of cerebellar tissue with preserved brainstem and supratentorial structures
Presence of cerebellar dysfunction signs such as ataxia, hypotonia, and dysmetria without other major brain malformations
Exclusion of other syndromic or genetic causes involving cerebellar hypoplasia or combined brain malformations
Genetic testing to exclude known mutations causing cerebellar hypoplasia or other neurodevelopmental disorders

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Complete absence of cerebellar tissue on MRI plus clinical evidence of cerebellar dysfunction and exclusion of other brain malformations
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis relies heavily on neuroimaging and clinical correlation; genetic testing aids in differential diagnosis.

laboratory: Genetic testing negative for known cerebellar hypoplasia mutations
imaging: MRI showing complete absence of cerebellar hemispheres and vermis
genetic: No pathogenic variants identified in common cerebellar development genes (e.g., RELN, VLDLR)

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of pontine hypoplasia on MRI
Cystic dilatation of the fourth ventricle
Partial cerebellar vermis hypoplasia rather than complete agenesis

redFlags: Severe feeding difficulties with failure to thrive
references: Parisi MA, Dobyns WB. Genetic and developmental aspects of cerebellar malformations. Curr Opin Neurol. 2003;16(2):111-9.
Poretti A, Boltshauser E. Cerebellar malformations and their genetic causes. Handb Clin Neurol. 2018;155:263-280.
